Class ChatShell

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.ssh.shell.ChatShell
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable, org.apache.sshd.server.command.Command, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectErrorStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectInputStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectOutputStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectStreamsAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandLifecycle, CommandContext
public class ChatShell extends Object implements org.apache.sshd.server.command.Command, Runnable, CommandContext
The ChatShell class is the VT100 shell for one SSH connection. It implements Command, Runnable, and CommandContext. It holds the line buffer, the escape mode, and the chat session. Command echo is green. Enter goes to the command processor or the model worker. The shell does not name the commands. Terminal bytes stay on this connection. // @aa-sdd L40 aa-sdd-source-prose.md#ChatShell

  • Constructor Details

    • ChatShell

      public ChatShell(ChatSession session, CommandProcessor processor, LlmService llmService, CasseroleProperties properties, String modelName, FormatRouter formatRouter, Lamina lamina, LlmRouter llmRouter, AmwpFacade amwpFacade)
      The constructor stores the session, the command processor, and the model services. Think starts empty. The family starts as ollama. Effort sending starts on. Stream starts off. Temperature starts at 1.0 and is not sent. The max-token value starts at 128000 and is not sent. The pool boot is a new random id. The mode starts as chat. The terminal width starts at 80. The escape timer is a daemon named casserole-esc. The spinner timer is a daemon named casserole-spinner.
      Parameters:
      session - The session is the chat state for this connection.
      processor - The processor is the command registry for this connection.
      llmService - The service is the Ollama boundary stored for this shell.
      properties - The properties are the server settings.
      modelName - The model name is the configured Ollama id used for status.
      formatRouter - The router formats a reply before it is written.
      lamina - The lamina submits the read loop and the model turn.
      llmRouter - The router is the provider map. The console turn calls AmwpFacade.completeTurn(String, AmwpToon.ExecuteBody, List) and does not take the execute permit.
      amwpFacade - The facade runs a console turn and a framed turn on the same path.

      public void start(org.apache.sshd.server.channel.ChannelSession channel, org.apache.sshd.server.Environment env) throws IOException
      The start method prepares the connection and submits the read loop. The SSH user name is read from the server session. A failure stores an empty name. The terminal width comes from parseColumns(Environment). Window-change listening starts. History and the console model are loaded. Bracketed paste is enabled. The welcome text is Welcome to Casserole chat, then the type, escape, Ctrl+C, and exit lines, then the paste line. A restored session writes the restored count and the user name. Any other session writes New session. The prompt is written. The read task is named casserole-chat-shell on Lane.SSH_IO.

    • run

      public void run()
      The run method reads SSH input until the stream ends or the shell exits. Each read uses a 1024 character buffer. Characters are handled under the shell lock, and one paint is flushed after the buffer. A clean end calls the exit callback with status 0. Any other failure calls it with status 1 and the exception message. An exit that is already underway does not call the callback.
      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • takeChar

      private void takeChar(char c) throws IOException
      The takeChar method applies one byte of the line editor. An escape in progress is appended until isCompleteEscapeSequence(StringBuilder) accepts it. A bare escape starts that sequence and the timer. Ctrl+C calls handleCtrlC(). Ctrl+A moves to the start. Ctrl+E moves to the end. Those two moves are skipped during a paste. Carriage return submits, or inserts a newline during a paste. A line feed inserts a soft newline when softReturn(char, boolean) is true. Backspace is byte 127 or byte 8. Ctrl+Z calls undoLine() outside a paste. A printable character is inserted, or appended during a paste. A sealed paste ignores printable characters until Enter, Ctrl+C, or backspace.
      Parameters:
      c - The character is one input byte.
      Throws:
      IOException - The method throws this exception when a write fails.

Command mode returns to chat when the session is active, and to idle when it is not. Any other mode becomes command mode. The prompt is written.

    • runLlmTurn

      private void runLlmTurn(String line, int maxMessages, int maxTokens, int managedTokens, int headCount)
      The runLlmTurn method builds the prompt, calls AmwpFacade.completeTurn(String, AmwpToon.ExecuteBody, List), and writes the reply. An exit or a cancel returns before the call and again before the write. A head over the allowance writes The head is over the allowance. Ephemeral is always false. The pool boot is this shell's boot. Grok fills the target as grok/ plus the id, plus stream, effort, think, burner cloud, temperature, and max tokens. Pool uses target pool and sets think to true only when the pool think string is true. Any other family uses ollama or ollama/ plus the model id, and copies the console think string. A user name that fails sanitizing throws an exception with the message invalid username. A null or blank reply throws The engine returned an empty reply. Success appends the user line and the assistant text, checkpoints, writes the reply header, and writes the prompt. A failure writes the formatted error and the prompt. The in-flight handle is cleared.
      Parameters:
      line - The line is the user text.
      maxMessages - The limit is the history cap for the prompt.
      maxTokens - The limit is the token cap for the prompt.
      managedTokens - The limit is the managed token cap for the prompt.
      headCount - The count is the head size for the prompt.
